function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – Key Points (2024)** | Topic | Summary | |-------|---------| | **Speed Limits** | • General speed limit on highways: 55–75 mph (varies by county).
• Rural interstate: 70 mph.
• Urban interstate: 65 mph.
• Speed limits on city streets: 25–35 mph unless posted otherwise. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑seat Requirements** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Children under 5 must be in a rear‑facing seat. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08 % or higher is illegal.
• For commercial drivers: 0.04 %.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • At uncontrolled intersections, vehicles on the right have priority.
• Stop signs: stop before the intersection and yield to traffic already in it. | | **School‑Zone Speed Limits** | • 20 mph during school hours; 25 mph during other times. | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Must signal and check mirrors/blind spots.
• Overtaking on the right is prohibited unless the vehicle ahead is turning left. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking within 20 ft of a crosswalk or intersection.
• No parking in front of a driveway. | | **Traffic Signal Violations** | • Running a red light or stop sign is a moving‑vehicle misdemeanor. | | **Vehicle Registration & Insurance** | • Must display valid registration and proof of insurance. | | **Towing & Tow‑away** | • Vehicles may be towed for parking violations, abandoned vehicles, or if they pose a hazard. | | **Special Vehicle Rules** | • Motorcycles: helmet required for riders under 18.
• Commercial vehicles: must follow specific weight and size regulations. | **Where to Find More Detailed Information** 1. **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** – Official rules, maps, and updates. 2. **Texas Transportation Code** – Statutory laws governing all aspects of driving. 3. **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** – Licensing, DUI enforcement, and safety resources. 4. **Local County Ordinances** – May have additional speed limits or parking rules. **Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas** - Always obey posted speed limits and traffic signs. - Keep a safe following distance (at least 2–3 seconds). - Use headlights from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather. - Stay alert for pedestrians, bicyclists, and school buses. - If you’re unfamiliar with a city’s traffic patterns, consider using a navigation app that updates real‑time traffic conditions. Feel free to ask if you need specifics on a particular rule or how to handle a particular driving scenario!
